title: Hummingbird Payments — edge case capture & dev scratchpad
content:
Context:
Hummingbird Payments (customer) is integrating Redwood's hosted API for the transaction-normalization assistant. They run a high-volume stream of webhook events from acquirers. Goal is to replace an on-prem rule engine with Redwood-based inference for merchant-normalized descriptions and category tagging. They are in a small pilot (1M tx/day).

Call summary (2024-03-14, 11:00 PST)
- Attendees: Priya (RWI CS), Marco (RWI Solutions Eng), Kelsey (RWI SRE), Samir Patel (Hummingbird Eng), Lian Zhou (Hummingbird PM)
- Main ask: low-latency normalization (p99 < 120ms), deterministic mappings for known merchants, graceful degradation if model times out, replay safety for dedup/ordering.
- Immediate blocker: occasional double-normalize bug (same transaction processed twice with differing categories) during bursts.

Observed behavior / reproduction notes
1) Probabilistic double-normalize (symptoms):
   - Happens during 1–2 minute bursts when inbound webhook concurrency spikes -> downstream consumer (Hummingbird) sees two normalized records for same transaction_id but with different "merchant_normalized" values (e.g., "Acme Grocery" vs "Acme Groceries").
   - Timestamps in Hummingbird logs show two distinct Redwood API calls for same txn_id with different request ids; upstream webhook delivered duplicate events (they claim) but our platform returned different results for each call.

2) Prelim hypothesis:
   - Non-determinism likely from model temperature / sampling for short prompts when merchant string is ambiguous.
   - Alternatively, caching prefix/KV cache not being applied consistently across concurrent requests (race between cache fill and read). Could lead to first request hitting model and second request being served from a partially-populated cache path that triggers a slightly different inference path.

3) Related infra signals we saw (from preliminary logs):
   - Several API calls at the same millisecond range mapped to different backend pods (pod-a vs pod-b) due to routing; model versions same (v1.3), but quantization config differs between a canary group (v1.3-q4_0) and stable (v1.3-q8_0) because of a recent rollout.
   - Pod metrics show model latency variance: pod-b median 95ms, pod-a median 130ms during the spike window. Pod-a also showing slightly higher GPU memory fragmentation warnings.

Important sample payload (redacted)
{
  "transaction_id": "txn_20240314_5591",
  "raw_description": "ACME GROCERY #124 SFO CA",
  "amount_cents": 8132,
  "merchant_metadata": {"acquirer": "FirstPay", "mcc": "5411"},
  "received_at": "2024-03-14T18:09:11Z"
}

Existing safeguards in integration:
- Hummingbird dedupe window: 30s. They use our request id (x-request-id) to dedupe, but because duplicate events have distinct request ids, dedupe misses.
- We offer a deterministic mode toggle in the API (sampling off) but they have it off for only ~40% of calls (was toggled for A/B test).

Immediate mitigations tried during call
- Turned deterministic mode on for the pilot route (Kelsey toggled via console) -> immediate drop in variance observed in sample set, but still saw one mismatched pair in 30 minutes.
- Suggested increase in dedupe window on Hummingbird side, but they worry about replay/backfill semantics.
- Rolled back canary quantized variant (Marco rolled config) to align all pods to v1.3-q8_0. After rollback, variance reduced but not eliminated.

Hypotheses prioritized (ranked)
1) Sampling/determinism: even 'deterministic' mode may have micro-behavior differences if prompt includes timestamp or transient tokens. Need to inspect prompt normalization flow (highest priority).
2) Cache race: prefix/KV cache not being atomically set across pods -> two concurrent requests could spawn two different inferences; check cache key composition and write-after-read windows.
3) Rollout heterogeneity: quantization differences causing slightly different logits leading to different top tokens for short merchant names.

Short tests to run (owner indicated)
- [Marco] Run a deterministic reproduction harness: send duplicates of sample payload with identical request id header and with different request ids; record outputs across 1000 trials, across time windows (spike emulation). (due 2024-03-20)
- [Kelsey] Extract cache-get/cache-set logs around affected timeframe for pod-a/pod-b, verify key collisions and latencies (due 2024-03-18).
- [Priya] Ask Hummingbird to temporarily route duplicates (same txn_id) to a single request id for 24 hours to help isolate system vs data duplication (due 2024-03-19).

Longer-term potential fixes
- Offer a per-route strong-determinism flag that: strips non-deterministic tokens from prompt, forces greedy decoding, and pins kernel/config across allocation group. (Product/ENG conversation)
- Add an idempotency API layer: allow caller-supplied idempotency_key that Redwood will cache mapping of key->inference result for a configurable TTL. (This reduces downstream dedupe burden.)
- Improve rollout policy to ensure quantized variant parity across any pods serving the same customer route (customer affinity routing).

Workarounds for Hummingbird (short-term)
- Use our deterministic_mode=true for all normalization calls until we fix root cause. Documented caveat: may slightly change edge-quality for ambiguous descriptions.
- Set dedupe window to 5 minutes for now (they accept greater latency for idempotent guarantee during pilot).

Open questions (for follow-up)
- Do Hummingbird webhook duplicates originate from the acquirer or their internal queue? Need audit from their infra (Samir to check).
- Is there any prompt-level metadata we add (timestamps, request-scoped counters) that could break determinism? Audit prompt builder code path.
- Can we repro locally with spike emulator using our current runtime flags (Marco) or is this emergent only in real cluster conditions?

Action items (owner, due)
- Marco: Run deterministic harness + 1k-dupe test, attach results to JIRA-3421 (due 2024-03-20).
- Kelsey: Pull cache logs + pod metrics for 2024-03-14 18:08–18:12Z and share (due 2024-03-18).
- Priya: Coordinate with Samir to get Hummingbird duplicate audit + share replay logs (due 2024-03-19).
- Marco/Priya: Draft short one-pager on idempotency API proposal for product review (due 2024-04-01).

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Remember to check that route-level rollout affinity exists — we have affinity for dedicated but not for hosted routes by default. Could be why different pods had different quantization.
- Consider adding a test to the rollout pipeline: run a tiny sample of deterministic text prompts across candidate quantized kernels and diff outputs for short token sequences (< 8 tokens) — flag if mismatch rate > 0.5%.
- If cache race confirmed, probably need to switch to compare-and-set for prefix cache writes. Watch out for perf regressions.

Appendix: quick debug log snippets (redacted)
[2024-03-14T18:09:11.103Z] req=abc123 pod=pod-a route=/normalize txn=txn_20240314_5591 prompt_len=46 latency_ms=142 result_hash=0x7a1f
[2024-03-14T18:09:11.104Z] req=def456 pod=pod-b route=/normalize txn=txn_20240314_5591 prompt_len=46 latency_ms=98 result_hash=0x7b2c

Both had model=v1.3 but pod-a kernel=jit-q8_0 pod-b kernel=jit-q4_0

—— end scratchpad — keep updated as tests come in.
